claim: *Coverage of model correspondence.* The modeled surface contains claims that can be checked mechanically and claims that require semantic judgment. Properties outside it have no model-based coverage. Engineering experience can move this boundary in either direction as newly important properties are represented or unnecessary distinctions are removed.
topology: Two separate horizontal arrows cross the gap between the outer modeled boundary and the outer unmodeled boundary. Removing an unnecessary distinction points outward; representing a newly consequential property points inward. Neither arrow is attached to the semantic-claims child region.
required_terms: No two owners for the same job
A failure mode outside the model
bw_encoding: Only the modeled territory receives a light 5% gray fill; the two claim regions and outside region stay white. Bold region names separate categories from regular descriptions and examples. Territory headings are 11 pt; all other text is 10 pt. Arrow labels and Example are italic.
redesign: Follow the author-supplied dynamic coverage reference: the modeled territory includes both mechanically decidable and judgment-dependent claims. Two opposing arrows expand or contract that territory. The outside label includes both never-modeled and retired distinctions.
alt: The modeled surface contains two regions: decidable claims checked mechanically, exemplified by no two owners for the same job, and semantic claims requiring judgment, exemplified by a meaningful result. Outside the modeled surface, unmodeled properties have no model-based coverage. An arrow from outside to the outer modeled boundary represents a newly consequential property; the opposing arrow removes an unnecessary distinction. Both changes apply to the modeled surface as a whole.
